transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’ve felt low and weighed down almost all the time for the last couple of years, and it just never really lifts. It's reached a point where I realize I can't just wait for it to get better on its own anymore.
Have you had any periods of at least 2 months during these last couple of years when you felt back to normal, or has the low mood been present most days without much break?

No, I haven't had anything close to a two-month break. This heavy, gray feeling has been there pretty much every single day since we moved up here over two years ago. I can't remember a single period where I felt back to normal for more than just a few days at a time.
Along with feeling low, have you also had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration most days?

Yes, my energy and concentration have been terrible. Even after eight hours of sleep, I feel like I'm wading through molasses and get exhausted by simple tasks like unloading the dishwasher. My brain is also in a constant fog, making it hard to focus on my work or even make simple decisions like what to wear in the morning.
Have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or is it mainly feeling sad and tired?

Yes, I've definitely lost interest in the things I used to love. Activities like precision baking, stargazing with my telescope, and neighborhood plant-swaps now just feel like exhausting obligations or chores. I just don't get any genuine joy out of them anymore.

Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where your depression got much worse all at once, with several symptoms becoming severe enough to clearly interfere with work, home life, or relationships?

No, I haven't really had a sudden, distinct two-week drop where things got much worse all at once. It has felt more like a constant, steady, and heavy low feeling that has been continuously present since it first started.
Have you ever had a period of at least a few days where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, talked more than normal, or felt overly confident or impulsive?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. I have never had periods of high energy, a decreased need for sleep, or felt impulsive. My state has just been consistently low and heavy instead.
During this low period, have you also often felt hopeless or had very low self-esteem, like you’re a failure or letting yourself or others down?

Yes, I feel incredibly hopeless about the future and can't picture things ever changing or feeling any different than this flat, numb state. I've even stopped making plans because it just feels pointless. I also carry a lot of guilt because I feel like I'm constantly letting down my spouse and failing to lead my research team effectively.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, thoughts of hurting yourself, or any suicidal thoughts?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. It's just that everything feels incredibly flat and pointless right now, but I have never wanted to harm myself.
Has this low mood and lack of interest been present for at least 2 years continuously, with no symptom-free period longer than 2 months?

Yes, it has been present continuously for just over two years, ever since we moved to the Bay Area. It has never let up for more than a few weeks at a time, and definitely never for a period as long as two months.
Have you ever had times when you heard or saw things other people couldn’t, or felt strongly that people were trying to harm you or that your thoughts were being controlled?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. I've never heard or seen things that weren't there, and I don't feel like anyone is trying to harm me or control my thoughts. It's just this constant, heavy numbness.
Have you ever had a medical problem or used alcohol, cannabis, or other substances that seemed to trigger or worsen this long-lasting low mood?
No, I don't really use alcohol, cannabis, or any other substances, so that hasn't been a factor. I'm also not aware of any medical conditions that could have triggered or worsened this low mood.
Has this low mood and loss of interest made it hard for you to keep up with work, home responsibilities, or relationships on a regular basis?

Yes, it has made things incredibly difficult. At work, my performance reviews have slipped because I'm missing deadlines and avoiding leading discussions, while at home, my spouse feels like they're living with a roommate since I constantly cancel plans, barely talk, and just zone out on my laptop in the evenings.
Did these symptoms start before age 21, or did they first begin later in adulthood?

They definitely started later in adulthood. It actually first began just over two years ago, when I was 37, right after we relocated to the Bay Area for my promotion. I didn't have these issues before that.
Have you had any periods during these two years when you felt noticeably better for several weeks, or has the low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day without much variation?

No, I haven't had any periods of several weeks where I felt noticeably better. The low mood and lack of interest have been there almost continuously for the entire two years. At most, I might have a day or two where the weight feels slightly less heavy, but it never truly lifts or stays away.
Have you ever had any symptom-free period lasting at least 2 months since this started, or has the low mood been present nearly every day the whole time?

No, I haven't had any symptom-free periods at all since this started. The heavy, low mood has been there nearly every single day since we moved two years ago. There has never been a break that lasted anywhere near two months.
Just to confirm, has this low mood and loss of interest been present most days for at least 2 years without any symptom-free period lasting 2 months or more?

Yes, that is absolutely correct. It has been present almost every single day for just over two years now, starting shortly after our move. There have been no long breaks at all, and the feeling has never let up for more than a few days at a time.
During this time, have you had trouble sleeping or sleeping too much most days?
I haven't really had trouble falling asleep or sleeping too much, and I usually get about eight hours of sleep a night. But despite that, I still wake up feeling completely exhausted anyway.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight during this time, such as eating much less or much more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?
No, I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or weight during this time. My eating habits and weight have stayed pretty much the same as they've always been.
During these two years, have you often felt very low in self-esteem or like a failure, or has it been more mainly low mood and loss of interest without those feelings?

It has been much more about the persistent low mood, emotional flatness, and a total loss of interest in things I used to love like baking or stargazing. While my perfectionistic side makes me worry about my performance slipping, the overwhelming feeling is just this heavy, gray numbness and physical exhaustion rather than deep self-loathing.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months in the last two years when these symptoms completely went away and you felt back to your usual self?

No, I definitely haven't had any period of two months where the symptoms went away. This heavy, low feeling has been pretty much continuous since we moved a little over two years ago. While there might be very brief moments where the weight feels slightly less heavy, it has never completely lifted or let me feel like my usual self.
During this same period, have you also often felt unusually irritable, tense, or worried most days?

Yes, I do feel very tense and worried, almost like I'm constantly bracing for something awful even when nothing is wrong. While there is definitely simmering tension at home with my spouse, it feels more like a constant state of dread and being shut down rather than outward irritability.
Do you find yourself worrying about many different things most days, and is it hard to control that worry even when there is no clear reason to be anxious?

No, I wouldn't say I experience constant, uncontrollable worry about many different things. While I do sometimes get that heavy, bracing sensation in my chest, my state is characterized much more by a flat, numb, and heavy feeling rather than active, anxious worrying.
Do you spend most days worrying about many different things and find it hard to control the worry, even when there is no clear reason to be anxious?

No, I don't really experience active, uncontrollable worrying about many different things. It is much more of a constant, heavy, flat feeling, though I do sometimes wake up with a vague, physical sense of bracing for something awful even when nothing specific is wrong.
Do you spend most days feeling anxious and worrying about many different things that you find hard to control, or is it mainly the persistent low mood and loss of interest without much active worry?

It is definitely the persistent low mood and loss of interest rather than active, uncontrollable worry. While I do sometimes feel like I'm physically bracing for something bad, the dominant experience is just feeling flat, weighed down, and unable to enjoy anything anymore.
Do you often find yourself worrying about many different things most days, and is that worry hard to control even when there is no clear reason to be anxious?

No, I don't really experience active, uncontrollable worrying about a lot of different things. It’s much more of a constant, heavy, flat feeling where I feel like I'm bracing for the worst, rather than actually spinning out with anxious thoughts.
Have you ever had a distinct period of at least 2 weeks where your symptoms became clearly worse all at once, with a more severe drop in mood or loss of interest than usual?

No, I haven't really experienced a sudden, distinct two-week period where things got significantly worse all at once. Instead, this heavy, low feeling has been pretty constant and steady ever since we moved two years ago. It just stays at this same flat, difficult level without any sharp drops.
Have you ever had a distinct 2-week period during these two years when your depression clearly got worse all at once, with more severe symptoms than your usual baseline?
No, I haven't noticed any distinct two-week period where things suddenly got much worse. It has really just been a steady, continuous, and heavy baseline of depression ever since we moved.

Have you ever had any distinct period of at least 2 weeks during these two years when your depression became clearly worse than your usual baseline, with symptoms severe enough to meet the full picture of major depression?

No, I haven't noticed any distinct period where things got significantly worse than my usual baseline. It has really just felt like a constant, steady weight and grayness the entire two years, without any obvious spikes or drops in how I feel.
During this time, have you noticed any changes in your movement or speech, like feeling slowed down, restless, or more sluggish than usual most days?

Yes, I definitely feel physically slowed down and sluggish, and doing simple tasks like unloading the dishwasher or walking up the stairs at the lab feels like wading through molasses. I haven't noticed any changes in my speech, though, and I haven't felt restless at all.

Have you had any periods of at least 2 weeks during the last two years when you felt clearly worse than your usual baseline, with a more intense depression or loss of interest than what you’ve described as your constant background state?

No, I haven't experienced any specific two-week periods where I felt significantly worse than my usual baseline. This heavy, gray feeling has been a very steady, continuous, and unchanging background state for the entire two years.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia): depressed mood and anhedonia nearly every day for just over 2 years, with no symptom-free period lasting 2 months or more, onset in adulthood, and associated low energy, poor concentration, hopelessness, guilt, psychomotor slowing, and clear functional impairment. There is no distinct 2-week major depressive episode, no mania/hypomania, and no psychotic symptoms. F32.0 was considered but is less likely because the course is chronic and continuous rather than a single mild depressive episode.
